title: 家人與家裡的事
subtitle: Talking about your family, celebrating birthdays, and shopping at the traditional market

vocab.gloss: family name; surname; to be surnamed

grammar.title: 姓 (surname) as a verb
grammar.pattern: Subject + 姓 + surname／Subject + 叫 + name
grammar.explanation: In Chinese, 姓 is a verb, not a noun: it means "to be surnamed". You say 我姓張 (I am surnamed Zhang) with no 是. Use 姓 with the family name only; use 叫 with the given name or the full name. To ask, say 你姓什麼？or the more polite 請問你姓什麼？The same works for family members: 我哥哥也姓張。
grammar.contrast: 姓 vs 叫: 姓 takes only the family name (我姓高), 叫 takes the given name or full name (我叫高小雨). If what follows is one syllable that is a family name, use 姓; if it is the whole name, use 叫.
grammar.common_error: Learners add 是 and say 我是姓張, or they put the full name after 姓 (我姓張小雨). Say 我姓張 or 我叫張小雨.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xìng Zhāng, wǒ gēge yě xìng Zhāng.
examples.gloss: My surname is Zhang; my older brother's surname is Zhang too.

examples.gloss: Her surname is Gao, and her husband's surname is Bai.

passage.title: 我家的人
passage.hanzi: 我姓張，我家人不少。哥哥在台北上班，每天搭捷運去公司，他的妻子在銀行工作。姐姐的丈夫是老師，他們就住在附近。妹妹還在讀書，常常騎腳踏車去學校。弟弟最愛喝珍珠奶茶。週末我們都回家吃飯，爸爸媽媽很高興。
passage.gloss: My surname is Zhang, and I have quite a few family members. My older brother works in Taipei and takes the MRT to the office every day; his wife works at a bank. My older sister's husband is a teacher, and they live right nearby. My younger sister is still studying and often rides her bike to school. My younger brother loves bubble tea most of all. On weekends we all come home for dinner, and Mom and Dad are very happy.

example.hanzi: 今天是我媽媽的生日，我們去餐廳吃飯。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān shì wǒ māma de shēngrì, wǒmen qù cāntīng chīfàn.
example.gloss: Today is my mom's birthday; we're going to a restaurant to eat.

example.hanzi: 朋友生日的時候，我們都會唱歌給他聽。
example.pinyin: Péngyǒu shēngrì de shíhòu, wǒmen dōu huì chànggē gěi tā tīng.
example.gloss: When a friend has a birthday, we all sing a song for him.

example.gloss: What color do you like best? I like white best.

example.pinyin: Zhè ge shǒubiǎo shì wǒ bàba sòng wǒ de.
example.gloss: This wristwatch was given to me by my dad.

grammar.title: 會 for learned skills（會／不會／很會）
grammar.pattern: Subject + (不)會 + Verb Phrase　/　Subject + 很會 + Verb Phrase
grammar.explanation: 會 says you have learned how to do something: 我會唱歌 "I can sing (I know how)." The negative is 不會, never 沒會. Put 很 in front (很會) and it means "is really good at": 她很會跳舞 "She's a great dancer." To ask, use 會不會 or add 嗎.
grammar.contrast: 會 vs 能: 會 is a skill you learned (我會跳舞), while 能 is about physical ability or the situation allowing it (我今天腳很痛，不能跳舞 — I know how, but not today). If you can replace it with "know how to," use 會; if it is "am able to right now," use 能.
grammar.common_error: Learners say 我能唱歌 when they mean "I know how to sing" — that sounds like "I'm permitted / physically able to sing." Also, don't say 我會跳舞得很好; the degree complement repeats the verb: 我跳舞跳得很好, or just say 我很會跳舞.

examples.hanzi: 我會唱歌，可是我不會跳舞。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ huì chànggē, kěshì wǒ bú huì tiàowǔ.
examples.gloss: I can sing, but I can't dance.

passage.title: 姐姐的生日
passage.hanzi: 上個週末是我姐姐的生日。我和哥哥先搭捷運去買一個手錶送她，她最喜歡的顏色是紅色，我們就買了一個紅色的。晚上全家人在家裡吃飯，飯後我們一起唱歌，媽媽還跳舞給我們看，大家都很高興。
passage.gloss: Last weekend was my older sister's birthday. My brother and I first took the MRT to buy a watch for her; her favorite color is red, so we bought a red one. In the evening the whole family ate at home, and after dinner we sang together. Mom even danced for us, and everyone was very happy.

example.gloss: Mom bought fish and vegetables at the morning market today.

example.gloss: The fruit here is too expensive; let's go look at another shop.

grammar.title: 問價錢：一公斤多少錢？
grammar.pattern: N + 一公斤／一斤 + 多少錢？（也可以說：一公斤 + N + 多少錢？）
grammar.explanation: In a Taiwanese market you ask the price by putting the amount (一公斤、一斤、一個) right before 多少錢. 多少 goes directly in front of 錢 with no 的 and no measure word. The noun can come first (西瓜一公斤多少錢？) or after the amount (一公斤西瓜多少錢？) — both are natural. To answer, just say the amount and the price: 一公斤八十塊。
grammar.contrast: 多少錢 vs. 幾塊錢：幾 must be followed by a measure word (幾塊錢、幾個), and it expects a small number you can guess; 多少 stands alone before 錢 and is the safe, neutral way to ask any price. So 雞蛋幾塊錢？ is fine for cheap eggs, but for a big bill you say 一共多少錢？
grammar.common_error: Learners say 「多少的錢」 or 「幾錢」. Never put 的 between 多少 and 錢, and never use 幾 without a measure word — 幾錢 is wrong, it must be 幾塊錢.

examples.hanzi: 老闆，西瓜一公斤多少錢？
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn, xīguā yì gōngjīn duōshǎo qián?

passage.title: 早市買菜
passage.hanzi: 週末早上，我和媽媽一起走路去附近的早市。早市裡有很多人，賣魚、賣菜的老闆都在叫：「來看看！」媽媽買了兩公斤羊肉、一斤雞蛋，還買了一個大西瓜。我說西瓜太貴了，媽媽笑著說：「這個很甜，一點都不貴。」回家以後，我們一起吃西瓜，真的很甜。
passage.gloss: On the weekend morning, Mom and I walked to the nearby morning market together. There were lots of people in the market, and the fish sellers and vegetable sellers were all calling out, "Come take a look!" Mom bought two kilos of mutton and a catty of eggs, and she also bought a big watermelon. I said the watermelon was too expensive, but Mom said with a smile, "This one is really sweet — it's not expensive at all." After we got home, we ate the watermelon together, and it really was sweet.
